name: Mount Eliza
intro: Mount Eliza is the Peninsula's northern threshold and, depending on how you read it, either its most affluent commuter suburb or its most underrated bay-side town. Both are true. The village strip on Mount Eliza Way is short, well-fed and self-aware  -  a few of the best independent cafés on the Peninsula are here  -  and the back streets fall down to a string of small bay beaches that locals have managed to keep more or less to themselves. Canadian Bay is the headline; Ranelagh has the postcard staircase; Sunnyside is the unofficial nudist beach for the brave. The town is independent-school country  -  Toorak, Peninsula Grammar, St Catherine's  -  which sets a particular weekend cadence: tennis-club mornings, café brunches, school-pickup-hour traffic. Stay here if you want a base that is closer to Melbourne than the rest of the Peninsula and quietly better-fed than its neighbours.
factualLede: Mount Eliza is an affluent bayside town on the Mornington Peninsula's northern Port Phillip coast, 50 km from Melbourne, anchored by a village café strip and a string of small bay beaches including Canadian Bay and Ranelagh.

heroImage.alt: Wooden beach-access staircase descending to Ranelagh Beach at Mount Eliza

tldr: Mount Eliza is the Peninsula's affluent northern gateway — a tight village strip with strong cafés, and a string of small bay beaches the rest of Melbourne has mostly missed.
Best for: brunch-driven day-trippers; families using Canadian Bay; anyone wanting Peninsula proximity without driving to Sorrento.
Signature experience: early walk to Canadian Bay, breakfast on the village strip, afternoon swim at Ranelagh.
A great day trip; an easy first night for a longer Peninsula weekend.
Closest Peninsula town to Melbourne — practical for a no-pack mid-week visit.
notFor: anyone chasing wineries on their doorstep
people who measure the Peninsula by Sorrento
stayDuration: a long day, or a first night
signature: The Peninsula's underrated northern village — quietly the best brunch strip and the closest bay beaches to Melbourne.
skip: Driving through to Mornington without stopping — Mount Eliza is more interesting than its reputation suggests.
bestDay: Walk to Canadian Bay at sunrise, breakfast on the village strip, late-morning swim at Ranelagh, lunch at one of the strip's small restaurants, beach again before the southerly arrives.
insiderNote: Park on Mount Eliza Way and walk the cliff-top path down to Canadian Bay — the approach is the best part of the visit.
